newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan clears second stock brokerage for China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan clears second stock brokerage for China.

text.p: TAIPEI, Nov 19 (Rueter) - Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it had approved Masterlink Securities Co's Hong Kong unit to set up a representative in Shanghai, the second Taiwan securities brokerage to do so.

"This becomes the second case after we approved Core Pacific's acquisition, through its Hong Kong subsidiary, of Shanghai Jinhua Consultancy Company in September," a commission official said by telephone.
The commission also approved Taiwan International Securities' plan to invest US$6.9 million in China-funded Shanghai Wanguo Securities in Hong Kong, the official said.
In July, Taiwan's economics ministry allowed overseas subsidiaries of local securities firms to set up representative offices, branches or subsidiaries in China.
Such communications have shown an increase since China's main Shanghai stock exchange president Yang Xianghai visited Taipei in July 1996.
Yang's visit marked a major breakthrough in financial ties between China and Taiwan, rivals since the end of a Chinese civil war in 1949.

Some 25,000 Taiwan firms have invested over US$20 billion in China and a few Taiwan-invested firms have managed to list stock on the mainland's Shenzhen and Shanghai bourses, but no Taiwan firms have direct stock listings there.
Restrictions on Chinese firms operating in Taiwan are even stricter. A few China-funded overseas firms have operations in Taiwan, but financial cooperation remains a distant prospect.
